proposed_title: WFP says an aerial attack destroyed food aid in South Kordofan
what_happened: A fresh Cloud GET retrieved UN News's exact 2 September 2026 report. It attributes to WFP the claim that an aerial attack on 30 August outside Dilling destroyed two marked trucks carrying 50 tonnes of food; the retrieved report does not identify the attacker.
key_facts: OFFICIAL_CLAIM: WFP, as reported by UN News, says two trucks and 50 metric tonnes of food were destroyed.
ESTIMATE: WFP says the load was sufficient to assist 5,800 people for one month.
OFFICIAL_CLAIM: WFP says it has recorded eight aerial attacks since January that damaged its premises and disrupted operations.
UNKNOWN: the retrieved report does not assign responsibility for the 30 August attack.

primary_sources.attribution: UN News report relaying World Food Programme statements
primary_sources.claim_supported: WFP's account of the destroyed shipment, quantities, intended beneficiaries and operational context
primary_sources.independence: UN-system reporting of a UN-agency claim; not independent forensic confirmation

contradictory_evidence: The retrieved source documents damage but does not identify a responsible party.
WFP's linked exact release could not be retrieved through the allowlisted Cloud tunnel, so it is not entered as evidence.
uncertainty: High confidence in what UN News attributes to WFP; perpetrator, weapon and independent damage verification remain unknown.
context: The conflict involves the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces, but that context does not support attributing this specific attack to either side.
why_it_matters: Destruction of a relief shipment can reduce assistance in an area facing severe food insecurity.
strategic_angle: HOLD for synthesis until an independent trail is retrieved; preserve WFP attribution and make no responsibility claim.
